nodes.label: Outbound Request Pending

nodes.description: Generate a 64-bit request_id for the outbound request (can be random, non-sequential)

nodes.label: Response Received
nodes.description: Response message received from peer with echoed request_id

nodes.label: Correlate Response to Request
nodes.description: Match incoming response directly to pending request using request_id without content inspection

nodes.description: Request successfully matched and response data available for processing

edges.label: Peer sends response with echoed request_id

nodes.description: Message conforms to eth/66 format specification

nodes.label: Process Message Payload

sub_graphs.title: EIP-2481: Concurrent Request State Management
sub_graphs.description: Models the state management for multiple simultaneous pending requests

nodes.label: No Pending Requests
nodes.description: Client has no outstanding requests awaiting responses

nodes.label: Pending Requests Active
nodes.description: Client has one or more requests awaiting responses

nodes.label: Add Request to Pending Set
nodes.description: Track new outbound request by request_id in pending set

nodes.label: Remove Request from Pending Set
nodes.description: Remove request from pending set after response correlation

nodes.label: Handle Duplicate Request ID
nodes.description: Handle case where response matches multiple pending requests with same ID

nodes.label: Response Potentially Misrouted
nodes.description: Response matched to wrong request due to duplicate request_id

ambiguities.text: Request IDs 'allow duplicates across request types' without specifying required handling behavior
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementations must handle duplicate IDs correctly by maintaining per-request-type tracking or using unique IDs in practice. This is an implementation detail left to clients.

ambiguities.text: No specification of timeout behavior for pending requests or cleanup of orphaned request tracking entries
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume implementations use reasonable timeouts (e.g., 30-60 seconds) and cleanup mechanisms for orphaned entries. This follows standard networking practices.

implicit_assumptions.description: Peers are expected to echo the request_id unchanged in their response
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious peers could send responses with incorrect request_ids, causing response misrouting or denial of service through confusion attacks

implicit_assumptions.description: An attacker cannot observe and replay responses with correct request_ids to different requests
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Man-in-the-middle could inject stale or forged responses to pending requests if they can observe the request_id

implicit_assumptions.description: Clients will implement proper tracking data structures that handle concurrent requests efficiently
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Memory exhaustion or performance degradation if tracking structures grow unbounded under request flooding
